note: Manual-mode scope questions. Selection: take all templates whose 'applies' condition holds, in 'order' ascending, until 15; if fewer than 5 apply, add the lowest-order unused 'always' templates. {topic} is replaced with the blog's topic. applies: always | scope_empty | audience_empty | has_files | web | academic | long | short.

templates.text: Who is the one reader you are writing "{topic}" for, and what should they understand or do afterwards?
What is your own position or angle on "{topic}"?
What is one real example, story or experience of yours that shows the point?
If a reader remembers only one sentence from this post, what should it be?
What should this post leave out?
What tone should this post have?

options: Stop when the point is made

templates.text: You didn't say who this is for. Who will read it, and what do they already know?
What exactly should the post cover, and what are the two or three points it must make?
Which parts of your attached documents matter most for this post?
Is anything in your attached documents confidential, unfinished or not for publication?
Are there websites, publications or people Claude should look at, or avoid, when researching this?
How recent should the evidence be?
Are there particular papers, authors or fields the post should draw on?
How much should the post lean on published research versus your own experience?
This is a long post. Which two or three sections deserve the most depth?
How should a long post be organized?
This is a short post. What single idea should it focus on?
